nh_clough_state_park.blurb: Clough State Park is in Weare, New Hampshire, on the east shore of Everett Lake, a reservoir on the Piscataquog River. The climbing here is bouldering on granite, spread over the North End, the South Side, the Island Boulder and a few roadside blocks. Problems run from V0 up to around V10, with most sitting in the V0 to V5 range and a thinner tail of harder lines. Expect crimpy lowball problems, roofs and tall slopey arete lines, plus a few cave problems that can stay damp. The rock is generally good, though flakes and small crimps can snap. Sun and shade are mixed through the boulders, and in warm months the mosquitoes are fierce, so bring repellent.

ut_stansbury_mountains.blurb: The Stansbury Mountains rise on the west side of the Tooele Valley, usually reached through Grantsville, about an hour west of Salt Lake City. South Willow Canyon is the heart of the range, with hard limestone sport climbing on outcrops along the canyon bottom and a few trad lines. The Valley of Zion is the next-largest area, and Stansbury Island adds a little bouldering. Grades run from easy up to 5.13, with the largest group at 5.10 and many more at 5.12 and 5.13. The upper narrows of South Willow are shady in summer, but can be crowded on weekends, so midweek is quieter and cooler. Deseret Peak is better known for its hiking trail than for routes.

co_black_canyon_of_the_gunnison.blurb: The Black Canyon of the Gunnison is a deep, narrow, steep-sided gorge near Montrose and Crawford in western Colorado, with walls roughly 1,800 feet deep. This is serious, adventurous traditional climbing, mostly long multi-pitch routes with up to 16 pitches, and rock that ranges from clean cracks to loose, chossy sections. Most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a smaller number of 5.8 and 5.9 lines, and ratings can feel stiff. A small amount of ice and some boulders are also here. The North Rim holds the most routes, while the South Rim has far fewer. The park describes it as unsuited to beginners. Prime seasons run from mid-April to early June and again from mid-September to early November.

wa_forest.blurb: The Forest is a bouldering zone in the Gold Bar Boulders, in the Reiter Foothills above the Skykomish Valley, set in the trees above the clear cut. It breaks into East, Central and West Forest, and nothing here is roped. Gold Bar's granite is gritty and durable, with rounded seams, knobs and blocky pinches. Problems run from V0 to about V9, though most are in the V0 to V5 range. The boulders are generally smaller than those out in the clear cut and they get very mossy, so a brush is useful. Across Gold Bar, shade keeps summer temperatures manageable but holds moisture, so spring and winter can stay wet, and fall is the prime season. Summer here brings plenty of mosquitoes.

wa_sunshine_wall.blurb: Sunshine Wall is a south-facing wall of basalt columns in Echo Basin, the small coulee just south of Frenchman Coulee near Vantage in central Washington. It holds the tallest pillars at Vantage, up to about 100 feet. The climbing is mostly trad on cracks, with a good number of bolted lines, including arete routes, and a few top-rope lines. Most routes sit between 5.8 and 5.11, with the 5.10s the biggest group. It is described as the perfect winter crag. The wall splits into the King Pins, Far End, Near End, Coyote Wall and Tilted Pillars. It is a busy place with something for most climbers.

ca_santee_boulders.blurb: Santee Boulders is a field of school-bus-sized boulders on a grassy hillside in Santee, in San Diego County. It is an easy-to-reach bouldering spot, best with a crash pad, and drawing both beginners and experienced climbers from around the city. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with some top-rope and a few trad and sport routes mixed in. The problems skew easy to moderate, with a lot of V0 to V3, though harder lines reach into the V10s and beyond. Roped routes run from about 5.8 to 5.12. The main concentrations are the Moby Dick, Dog Pile, Hillside and Synchronicity areas. Each boulder offers a different puzzle.
